Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment summary:
  - Acute severe headache for ~3 days, onset gradual at work; pain diffuse but mainly right periorbital, described as dull with intermittent sharper episodes, intensity ~8/10.
  - Associated features: photophobia (light hurts), transient visual “shooting lights” at onset, nausea/feeling sick (no vomiting), difficulty focusing. No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neuro deficits, no recent head trauma.
  - Family history: mother and sister with migraines.
  - Partial response: ibuprofen taken (≈3 tablets/day for 2 days) with minimal benefit; reduction of screen brightness provides some relief.
- Differential diagnoses consistent with transcript (from DDx):
  - Probable acute migraine — High likelihood: supported by unilateral-periorbital predominance, photophobia, transient visual phenomena (possible aura), nausea, family history, severe pain and poor response to OTC ibuprofen.
  - Tension-type headache / stress-related headache — Moderate likelihood: supported by dull, diffuse pain, prolonged screen/IT work and recent work stress, some prior headaches responding to ibuprofen.
  - Eyestrain / computer vision syndrome (refractive error-related) — Moderate–Low likelihood: supported by prolonged screen time, long-standing glasses use with no recent eye test, partial relief with reduced screen brightness; less likely given photophobia, visual phenomena and nausea.
- Contraindications / red flags: No red flag features documented (sudden thunderclap onset, neck stiffness, fever, focal neurology, repeated vomiting). DDx considered serious causes (SAH, dissection, intracranial mass, meningitis) but these are judged unlikely in the absence of objective red flags—no imaging or labs were ordered during this visit. No internal contradictions between transcript and DDx regarding likely primary diagnosis.

Management Plan
- Immediate treatment options discussed/offered:
  - Review ibuprofen dosing: clinician advised ibuprofen can be taken up to two tablets three times daily (patient previously took ~3 tablets/day). 
  - Alternative/stronger analgesics discussed; clinician offered prescription options including Naproxen (name offered; dose/route/frequency not documented), Paracetamol (name offered; dose/route/frequency not documented), and Codeine (name offered; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Advice to keep a headache diary to identify triggers and pattern.
  - Advice to reduce screen brightness and consider an eye test / repeat optometry review.
  - Safety netting: return or call sooner if headaches worsen, new visual loss, weakness, speech changes, or systemic illness develops.
  - Plan for follow-up: review in 1–2 weeks; consider prophylactic migraine medication if headaches become frequent.
- Prescriptions/medication given at visit: Not documented (options discussed; no specific prescription details recorded).

- Migraine headache (probable acute migraine) — High likelihood
  - Justification: Unilateral-predominant periorbital pain, photophobia, transient visual “shooting lights” (possible aura), nausea, strong family history of migraine, poor response to OTC ibuprofen.
- Tension-type headache / stress-related headache — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Dull, diffuse pain; prolonged screen/IT work; recent work stress; partial historical response to ibuprofen.
- Eyestrain / computer vision syndrome (refractive error-related) — Moderate–Low likelihood
  - Justification: Longstanding glasses use without recent eye test, heavy screen use, improvement with reduced screen brightness; less consistent with photophobia and nausea.
